newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian utilities tax based on cash not accruals.
newsitem.headline: Russian utilities tax based on cash not accruals.

text.p: Profit taxes for Russian utilities including gas monopoly RAO Gazprom and national and regional electricity companies will be based on cash rather than accruals methods of calculating profits, President Boris Yeltsin's press service said on Monday.
A decree signed by Yeltsin on December 29 said profits would be calculated on a cash basis for utilities when levying the tax.

Since October Russian companies have had to calculate profits on an accruals basis. Until then they could choose between cash and accruals. Profit calculations under Russian accounting standards are designed for the tax authorities rather than investors or business partners.
Gazprom and electricity companies have suffered heavily from a widespread failure of Russian customers to pay their bills.
